evidence.text: If there are any risk factors for early-onset neonatal infection (see box 1 on risk- factors for early-onset neonatal infection), or if there are clinical indicators of possible early-onset neonatal infection (see box 2 on clinical indicators of possible early-onset neonatal infection): • perform an immediate clinical assessment • review the maternal and neonatal history • carry out a physical examination of the baby, including an assessment of vital signs. [2021]

claims.text: The unrecorded maternal history and vital signs are normal, so infection has been excluded.

reasons: Claim C1 is not supported: the cited NICE guideline only instructs to perform assessment when risk factors or clinical indicators are present; it does not state that unrecorded maternal history and vital signs being normal excludes infection. The claim assumes normality and exclusion without evidence.

Claim C1 asserts infection is excluded based on assumed normal maternal history and vital signs, but maternal history is unknown and vital signs are not recorded; the guideline evidence only mandates assessment of risk factors and clinical indicators, not that normal findings exclude infection.
